subject: English Language
text: Either the students or the teacher ___ responsible for organising the rehearsal.
explanation: Rule: With 'either...or' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'teacher' is singular so use 'is'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the train arrived, we ___ waiting for two hours.
explanation: Rule: Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) shows an action continuing up to a past moment; use 'had been' here.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'The storm began to abate,' which word is closest in meaning to 'abate'?
explanation: Meaning contrast: 'abate' means 'to lessen or subside'; not 'intensify' or 'initiate' or 'contaminate'.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: 'He prefers to keep his cards ___.'
explanation: Idiom rule: 'keep one's cards close to one's chest' means to be secretive; 'close to his chest' matches the idiom.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following is the correct punctuation of the sentence: Ola said 'I'll see you at noon' ?
options: Ola said, "I'll see you at noon."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Quotation punctuation: commas precede a quotation tag and closing punctuation stays inside the quotation marks; option A is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'photograph'?
explanation: Stress pattern: 'photograph' is pronounced 'PHO-to-graph' with primary stress on the first syllable.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with the word 'rough'?
explanation: Phonology: 'rough' and 'tough' share the /ʌf/ sound; the others have different vowel or consonant sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following sentences functions primarily as a polite request?
options: Would you mind closing the window?
explanation: Pragmatics: 'Would you mind...' is a conventional polite request form; imperatives or commands are less polite.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: The results will be announced tomorrow.
Tomorrow will be announced the results.
The results will be being announced tomorrow.
explanation: Transformation rule: Object becomes subject and use 'will be' + past participle: 'The results will be announced tomorrow.' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: If she ___ earlier, she would not have missed the meeting.
explanation: Grammar rule: Third conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause ('had arrived') to express unreal past condition.

subject: English Language
text: Which version correctly punctuates this sentence: 'For the picnic we need plates cups and cutlery.'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
For the picnic, we need plates, cups, and cutlery.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Comma rules: introductory phrase takes a comma and list items require commas; option B supplies both correctly (serial comma accepted).

subject: English Language
text: In 'The manager's terse reply ended the debate,' what does 'terse' most nearly mean?
explanation: Lexical competence: 'terse' means brief and possibly curt or abrupt; 'curt' matches this meaning exactly.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the coach nor the players ___ ready for the match.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'players' is plural, so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By midnight, she ___ the report.
explanation: 'By' with a future time requires the future perfect: 'will have finished' indicates completion before midnight.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'The committee reached a consensus,' which word is closest in meaning to 'consensus'?
explanation: 'Consensus' means general agreement or common opinion; it is the opposite of 'conflict' and not a proposal or person.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: 'To burn the midnight ___.'
explanation: The idiom 'burn the midnight oil' means to work late into the night; 'oil' is the conventional collocation.

subject: English Language
text: Correctly punctuate the sentence: Maria replied I cannot accept the invitation.
options: Maria replied, "I cannot accept the invitation."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech requires a comma before the quotation and punctuation inside the closing quote: Maria replied, "I cannot accept the invitation."

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'economy'?
explanation: The pronunciation /ɪˈkɒnəmi/ places primary stress on the second syllable: e-CON-o-my.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with 'tough'?
explanation: 'Tough' (/tʌf/) rhymes with 'enough' (/ɪˈnʌf/). 'Cough' and 'bough' have different vowel sounds; 'though' is a different vowel combination.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence functions primarily as an apology?
options: Could you lend me a pen?
explanation: The phrase 'I'm sorry' explicitly expresses regret or apology; the other sentences perform requests, suggestions or statements.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The volunteers planted the trees last weekend.'
options: The trees were planted by the volunteers last weekend.
The trees were planting by the volunteers last weekend.
The volunteers were planted the trees last weekend.
The trees had been planted by the volunteers last weekend.
explanation: Past simple passive is formed with 'were' + past participle: 'The trees were planted by the volunteers last weekend.' Other options show wrong tense or word order.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct word: If he ___ more careful, he would have avoided the accident.
explanation: This conditional refers to an unreal past situation and uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause: 'If he had been more careful...' is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Which sentence correctly capitalises this book title: 'the sun also rises'?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Title case capitalises principal words including nouns and adverbs: 'The Sun Also Rises' correctly capitalises each main word.

subject: English Language
text: Read: 'Nana left at dawn to catch the first bus; she returned only at dusk.' What can you most reasonably infer?
explanation: Leaving at dawn and returning at dusk implies she was gone throughout the day; the sentence does not suggest missing the bus or sleeping.

subject: English Language
text: The captain, together with his teammates, ___ at the meeting this morning.
explanation: With 'together with' the verb agrees with the head noun 'The captain' (singular), so use singular 'was' rather than plural forms.

subject: English Language
text: By next month, the researchers ___ the preliminary data.
explanation: The phrase 'By next month' requires the future perfect ('will have' + past participle) for completion before a future time.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'The tutor commended the student,' which word is closest in meaning to 'commended'?
explanation: 'Commended' means to express approval or praise; it is the opposite of criticised or ignored and different from warned.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: 'Don't count your chickens before they ___.'
explanation: The proverb warns against assuming outcomes before they occur; the traditional completion is 'hatch', not the other verbs.

subject: English Language
text: Which version correctly punctuates the sentence: Amina said I have finished the assignment.
options: Amina said, 'I have finished the assignment.'
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Use a comma after the reporting clause and enclose the direct speech in quotation marks with the final full stop inside the quotes.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'banana'?
explanation: The standard pronunciation has primary stress on the second syllable: ba-NA-na; stress placement distinguishes pronunciation patterns.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with 'bough'?
explanation: 'Bough' is pronounced /baʊ/ and rhymes with 'cow' (/kaʊ/). 'Through', 'high', and 'again' have different vowel sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which of these utterances expresses condolence?
options: I am so sorry for your loss.
explanation: Condolence is expressing sympathy for someone's grief; 'I am so sorry for your loss' is an expression of sympathy.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The committee will approve the policy next week.'
options: The policy will be approved by the committee next week.
The policy will have been approved by the committee next week.
The policy will be approving by the committee next week.
The policy is approved by the committee next week.
explanation: Form passive with 'will be' + past participle: 'will be approved'. Option B is future perfect, C is ungrammatical, D wrong tense.

subject: English Language
text: How is this sentence reported? 'I will finish the essay tonight,' she said.
options: She said she will finish the essay that night.
She said she would finish the essay that night.
She said she would finish the essay tonight.
She said she will finish the essay tonight.
explanation: Direct speech with past reporting verb requires backshift: 'will' → 'would', and deictic 'tonight' changes to 'that night' in reported speech.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct preposition: She is accustomed ___ loud music.
explanation: The collocation is 'accustomed to' followed by a noun or gerund; 'accustomed for/with/of' are not the correct standard prepositions here.

subject: English Language
text: After the meeting, Kemi stayed behind to speak with the dean; the others left immediately. What can you most reasonably infer?
options: Kemi disagreed with the dean publicly.
The others were unhappy with the dean.
Kemi wanted a private conversation with the dean.
explanation: Staying behind to speak with the dean while others left suggests Kemi sought a private conversation; other options are not directly supported.

subject: English Language
text: Either the manager or the employees ___ aware of the change.
explanation: Verb agrees with the nearer subject: 'employees' is plural so use 'are'. Agreement with the closest noun is the standard rule.

subject: English Language
text: By the time the supervisor checked, Ahmed ___ assembling the parts for three hours.
explanation: Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) expresses an action continuing up to a past reference point; fits 'by the time' + past.

subject: English Language
text: In 'She exhibited composure during the crisis,' which word is closest in meaning to 'composure'?
explanation: Composure means calmness or poised control; 'poise' matches this. Anger and panic are opposites; sadness differs in meaning.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the idiom: 'He decided to bite the ___'.
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is the established idiom meaning to accept something unpleasant; the other words form different phrases or none.

subject: English Language
text: Correctly punctuate this sentence: Alima said I will arrive at six.
options: Alima said, "I will arrive at six."
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Use a comma before direct speech and place the final full stop inside the quotation marks: reporting verb + comma + quoted sentence is standard punctuation.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'development'?
explanation: The word 'development' has primary stress on the second syllable (de-VE-lop-ment); stress placement distinguishes meaning and pronunciation patterns.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with the word 'light'?
explanation: 'Light' and 'might' share the same vowel and final consonant sound (‑ight); rhyme requires matching stressed vowel and following sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which of the following sentences functions primarily as advice?
options: You must finish that report by noon.
Could you pass the salt, please?
What time does the meeting start?
You should see a doctor about the cough.
explanation: 'You should see a doctor' uses 'should' to recommend a course of action; the others perform obligation, request, or information functions.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They will deliver the package tomorrow.'
options: The package will be delivered tomorrow.
The package will have been delivered tomorrow.
explanation: Future simple passive is formed with 'will be' + past participle: 'will be delivered'. Other forms are active, incorrect tense, or ungrammatical for the context.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct preposition: She is proficient ___ Mandarin.
explanation: The collocation is 'proficient in' a language. 'Proficient at' is used for skills in some contexts, but standard usage for languages is 'in'.

subject: English Language
text: Fola arrived at the meeting soaked and her umbrella was broken. What is the most reasonable inference?
options: She had been swimming before arriving.
She did not own an umbrella.
explanation: Being soaked with a broken umbrella most reasonably implies recent heavy rain; the other options are unlikely or unsupported by the details given.

subject: English Language
text: If Olupe ___ the correct platform, he would have reached on time.
explanation: This is a past unreal conditional referring to a past counterfactual: use 'had' + past participle in the if-clause (third conditional form).

subject: English Language
text: Neither the students nor the tutor ___ available for consultation.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the noun nearest it (the tutor), so singular 'is' is required.

subject: English Language
text: By 9 pm they ___ the workshop.
explanation: Use future perfect for an action completed before a future time: 'will have finished' expresses completion by 9 pm.

subject: English Language
text: In the sentence 'Her explanation was lucid,' which word is closest in meaning to 'lucid'?
explanation: 'Lucid' means easily understood or clear; it contrasts with 'confusing' and is not simply 'brief' or 'elaborate'.

subject: English Language
text: To 'bite the bullet' means to ___ .
explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is an idiom meaning to face or endure a painful or difficult situation rather than avoid it.

subject: English Language
text: Which version correctly punctuates: Ayo asked Can you pass the salt?
options: Ayo asked, "Can you pass the salt?"
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Direct speech after a reporting verb needs a comma and quotation marks: Ayo asked, "Can you pass the salt?" (no extra period outside closing quote).

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable receives primary stress in the word 'documentary'?
explanation: Pronunciation places primary stress on the third syllable: doc-u-MEN-tary (/ˌdɒk.jəˈmen.tər.i/), so '-men-' is stressed.

subject: English Language
text: Which word rhymes with 'though'?
explanation: 'Though' rhymes with 'dough' (same /oʊ/ vowel sound); 'rough' and 'through' have different vowel/consonant sounds.

subject: English Language
text: Which utterance functions primarily as a polite request?
options: I wish the window were open.
The window needs to be opened.
Could you please open the window?
explanation: 'Could you please open the window?' uses a modal question and politeness marker 'please', marking it as a polite request.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They submitted the thesis last Friday.'
options: The thesis was submitted last Friday.
Last Friday they were submitted the thesis.
The thesis has been submitted last Friday.
explanation: Past simple active becomes past simple passive: 'They submitted the thesis' → 'The thesis was submitted last Friday.' Other options are ungrammatical or tense-mismatched.

subject: English Language
text: She was commended ___ her dedication.
explanation: 'Commend' with praise typically takes the preposition 'for' to indicate the reason: commended for her dedication.

subject: English Language
text: Kemi arrived at the lecture late but stayed until the end. What can you most reasonably infer?
options: She disliked the lecture and stayed by mistake.
She left before important points were made.
She valued the lecture enough to stay.
explanation: Arriving late yet remaining until the end suggests Kemi chose to stay, implying she valued the lecture; other options are not supported by the sentence.

subject: English Language
text: How is this sentence reported? 'I have sent the files,' he said.
options: He said he has sent the files.
He told he had sent the files.
He said that he will send the files.
He said he had sent the files.
explanation: When reporting past utterances, present perfect shifts to past perfect: 'I have sent' → 'he had sent' in reported speech.
